Our analysis, which is grounded in Bethe ansatz theory, reveals the phase diagram of the system for N value greater than 2 and finds that the system exhibits a continuous transition from a non-magnetic to a ferromagnetic phase as the interaction strength increases, accompanied by a specific type of scaling behavior. Our findings for N value equal to 2 are consistent with a previous study, which is interesting as they differ significantly from the predicted critical interaction strength for this phase transition based on a specific type of mean-field theory.

Recent advancements in the analysis of all-sky gamma-ray data collected by the Fermi Space Telescope have led to the discovery of 56 gamma-ray pulsars. By combining 37 months of gamma-ray light curves with data from 2008 to a maximum 3.1 years after transit detection, we conducted a comprehensive search for pulsars using the Green Bank Telescope. This analysis revealed 13 previously identified pulsars, as well as one newly discovered pulsar, PSR J183030.5+1928, which was confirmed through the detection of its radio and optical counterparts. Moreover, we also identified a pulsar, PSR J2332+51, that was previously detected by the EGRET telescope.

In the context of fractional quantum Hall states, we investigate the impact of an external magnetic field on systems with a range of low-energy excitations. Focusing specifically on the cases of Jain's Laughlin sequences near filling fractions $\nu = p/q + 1/m$, and the Moore-Read state at $\nu = 1/2$, we derive analytical solutions for the magnetoresistivity spectrum. These solutions are obtained by applying a magnetic field to the system and calculating the magnetoresistivity spectrum using the infinite-range repulsive model, which is an effective description of the low-energy excitations in these states. The results reveal that the magnetoresistivity spectrum consists of magnetorotons, which are collective excitations composed of pairs of quasiholes and quasiparticles. In the case of the Laughlin sequences, we observe the presence of multiple magnetorotons, resulting from the application of a magnetic field. These magnetorotons exhibit a range of low-energy dispersions, which are determined by the applied magnetic field. Furthermore, we derive spectral sum rules that are independent of the model and can be experimentally measured. Specifically, we derive the magnetorotons' low-energy dispersions and their respective degeneracies, which are key characteristics of the system's low-energy spectrum. The results obtained from our model are consistent with experimental data and provide a theoretical framework for understanding the observed magnetoresistance spectra in the integer quantum Hall edge channels.

The network of multi-disciplinary Extreme Energy Events (EEE) ground-based observatories, situated in Italy, Serbia, South Africa, and Vietnam, has been continuously collecting high-energy cosmic ray data since 2014, with the primary focus on studying extremely low-energy gamma rays below 1 TeV. Comprised of imaging water Cherenkov telescopes, featuring circular arrays of 256 cells at the base and 16 tubes above, the EEE telescopes utilize the novel patent-protected patented concept. The innovative design of the telescopes, featuring a unique combination of surface area and advanced data analysis methods, has allowed for the accurate identification of gamma rays and cosmic-ray events, with the correct classification of 70% of samples. The precise identification of hadronic and electromagnetic showers within these events has been achieved through the utilization of advanced machine learning algorithms, with the classification of 92% of the events being correct. The successful operation of the EEE telescopes in the southern hemisphere during the 2017-2018 solar minimum, when cosmic-ray rates peak, has been confirmed, with the resulting data showing a gamma/hadron discrimination efficiency of 92%.

The research focuses on solving the Cauchman problem for the Boltzmann equation with a cutoff, utilizing the Batalin-Gardiner-Strauss theorem, and demonstrates the stability of the equation's kernel under specific conditions. Initially, the initial data of the equation must meet certain regularity requirements, and it is proven that the solution to the equation exhibits exponential decay characteristics in terms of space and time.

To better understand how classifiers can withstand label noise, we develop a novel approach that represents classifiers as functions of both data and noise. This enables us to create a framework that examines classifier behavior under various noisy data conditions. We establish bounds on expected error rates and demonstrate how certain conditional independence properties can ensure robust classifiers with low error rates even when using noisy training data. This analysis provides insights into the effects of label noise and offers guidance for designing noise-resistant classifiers.

In the field extension ${\mathbb F}_{q^n}$, we examine cyclic orbit codes generated by extended cyclic polynomials with a right principal ideal generated by a orbit polynomial. The automorphism group of these codes is determined along with generalized automorphisms and isometries. By establishing an isometry between orbit codes and Reed-Solomon codes under specific conditions, we then define the generalized automorphisms for orbit codes in the context of the field extension ${\mathbb F}_q$.

A precise mass measurement of a star near the end of its main sequence has been achieved through photometric and spectroscopic observations of a star in the old open cluster M67, made possible by the K2 space telescope. This study utilizes data from K2 and Keck/Hect-HRS to obtain high-quality surface gravity and temperature values for the star. By combining these values with an isochrone fitting method, a precise mass measurement of $1.32\pm0.01$ M$_\odot$ was obtained for the star. This measurement is consistent with theoretical models when the cluster's age is set to approximately 2 or 3 billion years. Additionally, parallax and reddening data from Gaia and photometric measurements from K2 are used to investigate the cluster's distance and reddening. By analyzing the star's brightness, the team found that it is likely that the star is not a binary system. This study's results are used to discuss the accuracy of isochrone fitting and surface gravity measurements.

This research paper proves the completeness theorem for a set of special functions associated with the complex Schrödinger operator $ \mathscr{L}_c = -d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$, where $c$ is a non-zero real number, and $\alpha$ is a positive value greater than 1, over the interval $[0, \infty)$. The study also involves finding the asymptotic formulas for these special functions, as well as identifying the relationship between these functions and a related Bessel function. The work relies heavily on using the Liouville-Green method to derive its results.

To enhance the effectiveness of density-based smoothed particle hydrodynamics,
we introduce a new method for calculating gradients. Our approach involves
modifying the smoothing kernels to satisfy a partition of unity, which is then
used to develop a unique set of particles with distinct characteristics. By
further utilizing the Lagrange multipliers, our method demonstrates its ability
to satisfy both the partition of unity and the equation of state. In addition, we
derive the necessary constraints for the solution of the Lagrange multipliers,
resulting in an improved and conservative method for solving hydrodynamics
problems. Compared to other approaches, our method exhibits superior accuracy,
stability, and convergence in both one and two-dimensional problems, which are
further supported by a comprehensive set of numerical experiments.

Recent advancements in deep learning-based algorithms have successfully tackled the challenge of spectral super-resolution, producing high-quality estimates of low-resolution spectra from high-resolution counterparts. However, prior methods often overlook the relationship between individual pixels and frequently rely on the incorrect assumption that pixels are statistically independent. This paper proposes a novel deep function-mixture network (FMNet) that explicitly accounts for pixel values at each spectrum to capture their unique relationships. The proposed network consists of a multi-scale feature-mixture block (FSB) that combines features from multiple levels to generate spectral values and pixel-value-aware relationships. The FMNet also includes a multi-scale pixel-value estimation block (PSB) that produces precise spectral estimates. The proposed algorithm has been extensively tested and evaluated on various spectral datasets, yielding superior results compared to previous methods.

In the era of digital acceleration, there's a growing need for efficient geotagging to bridge the gap between physical and digital spaces. The issue arises because most current geotagging methods rely solely on visual cues, resulting in low accuracy when faced with objects in unfamiliar or changing contexts. To address this, our research introduces a pioneering context-aware geotagging framework capable of accurately locating objects in complex environments. This innovative system leverages a 3D map of surroundings to determine the most likely object location. To enhance geotagging, we integrated a novel 3D map builder that combines 3D object detection and geometric information to create comprehensive maps. The proposed system also incorporates a novel geotagging network that combines object and context cues to achieve accurate geotagging. To further improve performance, our framework incorporates a self-supervised learning strategy that leverages additional information from 3D maps. The proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in geotagging, showcasing its effectiveness with a 10% improvement on the NYU-DepthV2 dataset and a 5% improvement on the Matterport3D dataset.

The identification of dams and reservoirs within remote sensing images is a complex task, especially when using deep learning methods, which often overlook smaller reservoirs. This paper proposes a novel approach combining semantic segmentation and domain classification in two separate processing streams, enabling the generation of two distinct image outputs. The paper also introduces novel metrics for evaluating the performance of dam reservoir extraction models, specifically in the identification of dams, reservoir outlines, and number of reservoirs within predicted images. The proposed method has been tested using the new dam reservoir extraction dataset (DRED), which is based on the OpenAerialMap model, and achieved superior results, outperforming other leading approaches.

This study introduces the key concepts of quasilexico-fuzzy sets (QFS-sets) and discusses their characteristics, encompassing properties such as comparison, combination rules, operations like union and intersection, and operations of combination. Additionally, various attributes of QFS are examined, including properties of set operations, properties of a set, dimensionality, and representativeness, as well as classification, all of which have practical applications in decision-making and other related fields.

Predicting the type of a location mentioned in a social media post can aid users in planning activities. Current research focuses either on text-based features or images, overlooking the connection between a post's visual and written content. This study introduces POI-TYPE, a dataset for predicting a location's type based on both text and image provided in a tweet. A novel framework is proposed to tackle this task, incorporating multi-modal fusion and a transformer architecture to integrate the visual and linguistic aspects of a post, enhancing overall understanding and accuracy. Experimental results on POI-TYPE demonstrate that combining text and image yields better performance than relying solely on one type of multi-modal data.

Our research involves analyzing the correlation between spoken words and stock market outcomes in weekly- and monthly-scale transactions. This investigation is based on a language analysis of 200,000 transcripts from 6,400 U.S. corporate conferences between 2007 and 2018, where companies reported their quarterly profits to investors. To establish this correlation, we employed various methods, such as measuring the difference in the frequency of words used and their semantic importance. Additionally, we developed a predictive model to estimate future stock market fluctuations based on a company's previous four conference calls. This study demonstrates the potential of analyzing corporate statements in enhancing market forecasting capabilities.

In this research, we examine the complete coverage issue for wireless sensor networks with homogeneous or heterogeneous sensors, and limited line-of-sight (LOS) or line-of-sight-blocked (LOSBlk) communication ranges. We focus on sensors with limited communication range, and develop novel coverage definitions for both types of networks. By analyzing the relationship between sensor coverage and network connectivity, we demonstrate that complete coverage implies network connectivity. We then prove that determining the minimum number of sensors needed for complete coverage and connectivity is NP-hard in both homogeneous and heterogeneous cases. Based on this proof, we develop a greedy algorithm to find an approximate solution for limited-range sensors in both network types. We also propose a sensor deployment strategy with guaranteed coverage and connectivity for the general case of sensors with varying communication ranges.

A quantum eigenstate-based approach for target solutions in quantum linear systems is developed, utilizing Householder transformations. This method is based on the recognition that a specific relationship exists between a quantum eigenstate and its corresponding solution, which can be leveraged to filter the desired outcome. A novel algorithm is presented, utilizing a basis of polynomials of Hermitian matrices, to represent the eigenstate and eliminate all other options. The algorithm demonstrates superiority over previous methods in solving quantum systems, with optimal coefficients requiring fewer qubits than previously proposed methods, and can be implemented with a comparable number of gates.

We investigate the behavior of compact gauged baby skyrmions under varying density and temperature conditions, and in the presence of a magnetic field, within a nonlinear environment. The study reveals that increasing the density of solitons results in more uniform radial distribution and reduced magnetic energy, but as the radial thickness grows, the solitons spread and form larger areas in the radial direction. The topological charge of the compact gauged baby skyrmions grows linearly with the radial thickness at low temperatures, but this growth accelerates as the temperature increases. Additionally, the radial thickness has a significant impact on the soliton's energy, leading to higher energy levels, particularly in the presence of a strong magnetic field. The study also shows that increasing the radial thickness leads to more uniform soliton profiles within the medium.

The Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) is a widely used framework for studying new interactions beyond established physics. It enables researchers to analyze the impact of various effects, such as electroweak and strong corrections, as well as quantum effects like loop loops. By studying specific operators, scientists can gain insights into novel interactions and underlying physics, such as Higgs interactions with fermions and gauge boson interactions. Recent research has focused on combining data from different experiments to understand Higgs coupling behavior and Higgs diphoton decay mechanisms. Future research at the ILC, HL-LHC, and CLIC will provide more accurate measurements of Higgs and gauge boson physics, and may uncover new physics related to heavy or light particles.

We've successfully developed and tested a rotating diamond nuclear gyroscope based on nitrogen-vacancy centers. By using dynamic nuclear polarization enhancement, our system achieved high accuracy and efficiency. The diamond gyroscope was mounted on a precision motor and accurately measured angles of 0.23 and 0.17 degrees within a 10-minute dataset. The resulting precision, a minimum bias angle error of 0.04 degrees, was significantly lower than our measurement accuracy, suggesting potential for enhanced performance through optimization. Additionally, we explored the gyroscope's sensitivity to external magnetic fields and temperature fluctuations, and investigated the impact of nitrogen-vacancy center spin relaxation on measurement precision.

Whole-cell simulations aim to create comprehensive, mechanistic models of cellular function by integrating all components of cell physiology. Despite significant advancements in the past decade, combining these advancements into a unified whole-cell model has been difficult. With the advent of new methods and tools such as the Chaste whole-cell simulator, it is now feasible to develop integrated whole-cell models. This paper introduces key concepts in whole-cell modeling, describes recent technological breakthroughs and their applications, and explores the essential characteristics of future whole-cell models.

Mobile phone cameras are becoming a crucial source for gathering visual data in the world. This project delves into the potential of utilizing non-structured, real-world mobile view collections for object image search tasks. A novel approach called Mobile Multi-View Object Image Search (MMVOIS) is proposed to tackle this problem. The proposed method, M3OS, first creates a database consisting of 10 multi-view object instances. It then employs a novel matching strategy for object image search queries. The results of M3OS demonstrate its effectiveness in outperforming existing object image search systems and highlight its potential as a pioneering new model for object image search.

Implementing cutting-edge seizure prediction for patients could greatly improve their quality of life but remains a complex challenge.  Developing a reliable system for predicting seizures from long-term patient monitoring requires a machine learning model that is both efficient and reliable.  High-dimensional data collected during these monitoring sessions often results in a large number of features, making it difficult to identify those most relevant to seizure detection.  The hyperdimensional (HD) computing approach has been shown to be effective in learning high-dimensional representations of data that can be used for a variety of classification tasks.  We explore the use of HD computing for building high-dimensional representations of electroencephalogram (EEG) data that can be used to identify seizures.  We compare the performance of our HD model with a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) classifier and find that it significantly outperforms the LDA classifier in terms of classification accuracy.  Additionally, we demonstrate that the HD model is resistant to noise and data degradation.  Our results show that the HD model has the potential to be a powerful tool for predicting seizures in patients.

Future Deci-hertz gravitational wave detectors, capable of detecting binary black hole systems at various redshifts, can serve as "standard sirens" for cosmology. We propose that these detectors can provide an independent validation method for the accuracy of cosmological models by analyzing the redshifts of the binary black hole systems they detect. To achieve this, we utilize the Bayesian model comparison method to determine the most suitable cosmological model. We also investigate the potential for the detectors to obtain precise measurements of the Hubble constant, with our analysis suggesting that the current design of the A+ detector could yield a precision of approximately 1.4% for nearby binary black hole systems. We then developed a model to forecast the potential constraints on the Hubble constant that future detectors could obtain based on the number and redshift distribution of the binary black hole systems they detect. We also discuss the potential for the detectors to make precise measurements of other cosmological parameters, such as the dark energy equation of state, with our analysis indicating that the current design of the A+ detector could yield a precision of approximately 0.04 for D+L.

This study presents an enhanced version of the QALD-9 dataset consisting of 1,754 questions related to DBpedia in nine languages, along with corresponding answers sourced from Wikidata. Building on previous translations of QALD-7 into English, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch, Chinese, Japanese, and Swedish, the extended dataset now includes native speaker translations of the original English answers and their corresponding answers in the target languages. Leveraging native speakers for translation assessment allows for a more precise evaluation of the task, particularly in the context of Question Answering over linked data. All relevant data has been made publicly available on the QALD website at [qald.io/qald-9/], alongside the QALD-9 task guidelines.

Human decision-making is shaped by various cognitive processes, and to replicate this complexity, we propose an innovative reinforcement learning (RL) agent that utilizes a novel policy learning method. This policy leverages a unique value estimation approach that considers multiple perspectives, viewed through the lens of a virtual camera, to provide a more comprehensive estimation of the state value. By employing a self-supervised learning strategy, the proposed method efficiently processes sensory inputs and produces more accurate value estimates, outperforming traditional RL methods in diverse environments, including those with partial information and episodic and non-episodic scenarios.

The influence of medical image modality biases on the performance of classification algorithms is significant.  To address this issue, we have developed a framework that enables the detection of intrinsic bias in medical image datasets through the application of statistical tests.  The framework initially employs a statistical test to identify bias at a dataset level, and subsequently, if bias is detected, local bias hotspots are identified by applying the same statistical test to individual image patches.  Through experimentation with multiple datasets, we have found that the proposed method effectively detects intrinsic subpopulations, and in doing so, intrinsic bias is identified in medical datasets.

The impact of noisy training data on metric learning is substantial. A widely used K-NN based loss in metric learning is particularly susceptible to data inaccuracies due to its reliance on a limited number of neighbors. To mitigate this shortcoming, we introduce a new method, called Smooth Proxy-Anchor Loss, by modifying the K-NN based loss into a proxy-based loss through a novel technique. The proposed approach yields two losses: one that is robust to data noise and another that retains the benefits of the original loss while accounting for noisy data. Experimental results confirm that our methods outperform the K-NN based loss in both cases. Furthermore, our methods deliver comparable or superior performance than the best existing methods in several benchmark datasets.

The 2PCF is a powerful tool for studying dark matter clustering in cosmology, but it's typically limited by the accuracy of our understanding of the galaxy bias. However, the bias is not uniform across all scales, and it's often influenced by galaxy properties. To overcome these limitations, we've developed a new approach, which involves analyzing the weighted power spectrum by incorporating galaxy mass-luminosity relations. By combining this method with the 2PCF, we've been able to significantly improve our constraints on the galaxy bias, particularly for galaxies with lower luminosities. Our study on the MaNGA dataset reveals that our new approach provides more accurate results than the traditional 2PCF method, particularly at lower redshifts. Furthermore, we've been able to derive consistent constraints on the matter density using different galaxy samples, even though they exhibit different luminosity-dependent biases. Our findings suggest that this new approach can be used to improve constraints on the matter density, particularly when combined with other cosmological probes.

Recent NMR studies in superconducting Kagome quantum devices have revealed potential SO(5) spin fluctuation superconductivity. This phenomenon, characterized by a non-local order spanning multiple sites, is challenging to model using standard Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. We propose an integrable model of superconducting Kagome lattices that captures the key features of SO(5) superconductivity. Our model reveals unique properties such as the distribution of Cooper pairs between local and non-local channels, dynamic spin susceptibility and the nature of the ground state.

Recent advancements in avalanche photodiodes have been reviewed, placing particular emphasis on the innovative concepts of MAPD and MAPD-based photodetectors. Following an introduction to the fundamental operating principles of avalanche multiplication and the functioning of standard p-n and p-i-n photodetectors, the theoretical framework and operational mechanism of MAPD are thoroughly examined. On the basis of MAPD, a range of innovative photodetector structures are developed, encompassing inverse p-i-n, p-n, p-n traveling-wave, p-n resonant-cavity, p-n nanostructured, p-n nanowire, and p-n nanotube photodetectors. These devices offer enhanced performance capabilities, enabling them to operate under extreme conditions of high input power, temperature fluctuations, and radiation exposure. Ultimately, the potential applications and future research directions of MAPD and MAPD-based photodetectors are considered, holding promise for breakthroughs in fields like optoelectronics, photonics, quantum computing, and quantum optics.

This study examines the properties of sectional genera function $g_{\mathfrak m}^s$, specifically with respect to conditions where this function remains non-decreasing or increases at a consistent rate, when the local ring $A$ meets specific criteria for Cohen-Macaulay rings or localized rings with non-regular localizations. Our work also explores how these conditions relate to the Cohen-Macaulay and Gorenstein properties of rings. Moreover, we demonstrate the applicability of our findings to graded and non-graded situations.

A comprehensive investigation of Aurivillius bismuthates' magnetic properties at high pressures is currently lacking. To address this, researchers conducted a study on Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ (BFTO) single crystals using nuclear forward scattering (NFS) and transport measurements, with the goal of exploring the phase transitions triggered by high pressure. The experiment revealed that BFTO's tetragonal phase remains stable up to 7 GPa, with a slight reduction in unit-cell volume. The study found that BFTO's tetragonal phase exhibits antiferromagnetic ordering below 180 K. The NFS data further showed that applying pressure to BFTO results in a 2.5% decrease in the c-axis lattice parameter, indicating a strong pressure-induced effect on BFTO's magnetic structure. The NFS data collected above 180 K exhibited a characteristic pattern attributed to critical fluctuations, with the experiment providing valuable insights into BFTO's magnetic properties at high pressure.

A quantitative method is proposed to assess the performance of different broker algorithms under uncertain conditions, represented by probability distributions for security prices and trading volumes. This approach enables a detailed analysis of trading costs for each algorithm through probability distributions, allowing for the calculation of the algorithm with the lowest average and highest trading risk. Additionally, a method is developed to compare the effectiveness of these algorithms through the calculation of their relative rankings and probability distributions, including the confidence interval associated with each ranking. This method is demonstrated using a case study that includes five commonly employed algorithms: execution strategies such as market orders, immediate execution, price improvement, instantaneous execution, and limit orders with immediate execution. The results show that immediate execution and limit orders with immediate execution exhibit similar performance in terms of average and highest trading costs, with immediate execution having a lower average cost but higher highest risk, whereas the price improvement strategy consistently yields the lowest average and highest trading costs with the highest risk.

We have developed a fully adjustable system for filtering specific wavelengths. This design combines a ring-shaped light source with two adjustable components, allowing for a wide range of frequency options. Our device uses unique properties of the optical interface between two materials to enhance performance. In our experiments, we achieved an impressive 95% efficiency in coupling light between the two components, resulting in a highly precise and efficient filtering system. This technology has the potential to simplify the development of advanced optical communication systems by enabling the creation of highly customized light filters.

Public health interventions significantly impact the lives of a community's members, yet their effectiveness is often assessed through time-consuming, resource-intensive methods, such as traditional surveys. In contrast, social media and search engine data provide an alternative for evaluating these interventions with greater efficiency and resource availability. This study introduces a novel approach to assessing the effectiveness of vaccination campaigns using Google Search data. It demonstrates the feasibility of this approach by analyzing the impact of the 2019-2020 COVID-19 vaccination campaign in Israel, using metrics such as vaccine hesitancy and adoption rates among individuals aged 18 and above. The study's results show that the vaccination campaign reduced COVID-19-related search queries by 13% across the entire population, with disparities in search trends observed among various demographic groups. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the factors influencing public willingness to receive vaccinations and offers a method for rapidly assessing their effectiveness, enabling policymakers to make evidence-based decisions in a timely manner.

Effective image compression for both lossless and lossy applications necessitates a deep understanding of image characteristics and compression principles. Traditional methods often rely on extensive training, necessitating extensive computations. To achieve both high compression ratios and competitive prediction performance, we propose PILC, a novel end-to-end network that utilizes a neural lossless framework. By leveraging a GPU-optimized design, PILC has been implemented on an NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU, demonstrating superior performance in comparison to existing lossless and lossy compression methods. Notably, PILC outperforms the state-of-the-art lossy JPEG Image Standard (Image) in terms of compression ratio while matching its prediction accuracy on standard benchmark datasets.

Using 3.0 fb^-1 of LHCb data collected at various collision energies, the experiment observes a significant $B^{+}$ decay to $D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$ for the first time. With 3.7 standard deviations of confidence, the analysis determines branching fractions, finding them to be 7.1 ± 1.4 (stat) ± 1. (syst) × 10^-6 for $B^{+}$ decay to $D_s^{+}K$. In comparison, the branching fraction of $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}\pi^{+}K^{-}$ is measured at 11.0 ± 0.7 (stat) ± 0.4 (syst) × 10^-5.

Optimal transport distances are widely used in data analysis, but they become unreliable when data sets contain outlying measurements. To address this, we introduce a way to make these distances more robust by detecting and down-weighting outliers based on predicted values. This approach has several benefits, including improved performance in identifying outliers, better results in supervised learning tasks, and improved robustness to outliers in unsupervised learning methods. We also present different techniques for outlier detection and demonstrate the effectiveness of our robust transport distances through experiments on public data sets.

This paper proposes an innovative framework for developing AI teammates that work closely with humans in decision-making scenarios, where both parties share goals, communicate effectively, and collaborate seamlessly. To achieve this, we first establish a comprehensive framework for human decision-making patterns. Next, we develop a novel method for designing AI teammates that work in harmony with humans, using reinforcement learning to model optimal strategies. We then outline a practical approach to train the AI teammates within the framework. Finally, we demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through a case study in a simulated military command scenario, where the AI learns to assist a human commander plan operations. Our results show that the AI teammates can enhance the human's decision-making capabilities, ultimately leading to better mission outcomes.

In supersymmetric models with a large number of supersymmetry multiplets, the spectrum is significantly modified at one-loop order. Our analysis focuses on the basic features of these models at both perturbative and non-perturbative levels, as well as their implications for the spectrum and the potential mass differences between different states. Furthermore, we explore the possibility of observing these models in particle colliders, specifically the Large Hadron Collider, and discuss how certain models can be distinguished from the standard supersymmetric model through their unique decay patterns. Additionally, we discuss the relevance of these models in certain cosmological contexts.

To optimize visual analytics tools for specific tasks and user groups, it's crucial to understand the underlying characteristics of the users and how they impact interactions with these systems. Building on the concept of performance differences, we conducted a study to investigate whether users from varying fields and backgrounds exhibit notable variations in task performance, with a particular focus on the variation in performance based on spatial abilities. We gathered data from 160 participants through a visual classification task and used spatial ability as a key variable of interest. The study revealed that field had the strongest correlation with task performance, with domain-specific differences being more significant than the participants' level of formal education. Moreover, we discovered a moderate connection between spatial ability and task performance. The analysis also showed that users' choices for task features, where they placed the labels, varied based on their field and spatial ability, highlighting the potential of visual ability as a criterion for personalizing visual analytics systems to enhance the users' experience.

We've developed a novel proof strategy for inductive proofs with theories that rely on the concept of clause set cycles. Our approach involves defining a new, sound, and complete proof calculus for induction that directly utilizes clause set cycles. Notably, we've achieved a 2-way implication between soundness/completeness of a substructural logic for clause set cycles and the corresponding properties of the original underlying logic. Furthermore, we've been able to adapt our method to several prominent theories, such as order relations, numerical comparison, and arithmetic.

Graph-based data is widespread across varied domains such as social networks, language, and biology. Graph Text Retrieval aims to identify documents containing a given graph within a collection of documents. Current methods for text-based Graph Retrieval produce a ranked list of documents by matching individual graph vertices to text phrases. However, accurately determining the matching can be challenging due to the potential for vertex misidentification. To address this issue, we have developed a new approach that utilizes a matching model to identify the optimal set of paired vertices from a pre-trained language model. Our approach, called Matching Models for Graph Retrieval, achieves superior results compared to existing methods, with significant gains of up to 18.9% in terms of MAP@20 on two benchmark datasets.

Recent studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of pre-trained neural networks in improving transient modeling capabilities. Building upon these concepts, this work proposes a novel approach that leverages pre-trained networks to develop accurate transient models by integrating pre-conditioning techniques and a supervised learning mechanism. The resulting method, which combines pre-trained networks with a gradient boosting algorithm, yields significant improvements in forecasting accuracy and offers improved computational efficiency. Comprehensive evaluations across four real-world datasets and three distinct forecasting tasks confirm the superiority of our approach over established baselines and highlight its potential applications in transient data-driven modeling.

In countries where electricity demand significantly surpasses supply, the allocation of available electricity often serves as a benchmark for evaluating fairness in distribution. The existing literature on the topic of electricity distribution is scarce, and most studies rely on theoretical approaches to address the issue. This research aims to bridge this knowledge gap by developing a comprehensive framework for evaluating and distributing electricity with consideration for fairness standards. Building on existing concepts in the field of fair division, this study introduces novel algorithms and metrics designed to mitigate power disparities between producers and consumers. The proposed metrics are based on the idea of comparing the total value generated by each group, and the resulting algorithms aim to maximize this value. The study also explores the feasibility of maximizing the value of specific fairness measures, such as minimizing the advantage of the weaker party, and the maximum minimum share achievable. The study provides theoretical evidence supporting the effectiveness of the proposed methods, and a practical implementation of these concepts is applied to a real-world scenario involving electricity allocation to Nigerian states.

A dataset of event coreference resolution has been developed to connect various reports on the same incident. Based on the event ontology, which covers contentious politics events, this dataset is relevant to multiple disciplines including social media studies, crisis informatics, and the study of mass events. The dataset is accompanied by a method for producing and utilizing coreference datasets and examines the relationship between event coreference resolution and annotation tasks in the field of humanities.

The Complementarity Knapsack Problem, characterized by real-valued variables and complementarity constraints between pairs, has its polyhedral properties explored. Two new families of cutting-planes are identified: For nonnegative variables, Gomory cuts and outside-simplex cuts are found, and when variables can take any real value, linear and extended-weak-cobra cuts emerge as useful tools.

This paper defines and explores the concepts of generalized $(m,n)$-Jordan derivations and centralizers within semiprime rings. We establish that under certain conditions, any $(m,n)$-Jordan derivation or centralizer is generalized for that particular case. Our proof also demonstrates that the product of two generalized $(m,n)$-Jordan derivations results in two distinct derivations, each with its own distinct centers. We further demonstrate the imprimitivity of a prime ring when it contains a non-zero generalized $(m,n)$-derivation.

It is demonstrated that Weinberg's 2-factor scattering amplitude arises inherently within helicity constraints, arising as the linear combination of two coalescing two-gauge helicity constraints that share a common term. Furthermore, it is shown that this 2-factor amplitude is also the solution to a triple integral problem where the gauge invariance is subtly linked to the behavior of the integrand as the momentum becomes infinite.

We explore a broader application of transversal sets in nonlinear projections, originating from a problem concerning nonlinear projections introduced by E. Glueck, in collaboration with A. Grushka and A. Szpiro, leveraging properties of a specific family of nonlinear projections. This concept is connected to a problem related to a particular curve's path length that generalizes the Favard length. The problem involves finding the optimal path length between two points within a confined area with multiple convex regions. This research focuses on continuous functions that map within these regions, and our findings establish the existence of certain specific paths that achieve the minimum path length. Additionally, our results demonstrate the existence of a single path that achieves the minimum path length among all possible paths, and establish a relationship between the existence of a general transversal set and the specific set of minimizing paths.

We introduce a new framework that enables efficient guided policy search (GPS) for complex control systems with unknown dynamics. The framework involves imitating tube model predictive controllers (MPC) that are robust to system discrepancies to create policies that maintain stability even in the face of uncertainty. To facilitate real-time implementation, we develop a more efficient approach by using a piecewise linear approximation of the tube to reduce the complexity of the MPC problem. The resulting policies are then used as initial conditions for a GPS algorithm, which refines and stabilizes the system within the tube. Through simulations of a quadrotor planar landing scenario, we found that the proposed approach can significantly reduce the MPC problem size while achieving robust performance when imitated. Furthermore, we found that the resulting GPS algorithm converges efficiently to optimal policies, even when starting from a large imitation area, and outperforms traditional GPS methods in stability and efficiency.

The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect resulting from by skew scattering is typically characterized by its second-order nature. However, in this work, we explore the potential for a third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect caused by a specific type of band structure, where a small energy difference between two bands enables the conversion of a photon. This third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect is distinct in that it does not rely on skew scattering. A general framework for calculating the third-order intrinsic anomalous Hall effect is established, drawing on the principles of the classical theory of commensurability. This framework yields several notable features, including the potential to control the effect with magnetic fields and to enhance it with materials featuring strong spin-orbit coupling.

The code's call graph maps out the interactions between functions in an application's source code. A collection of such graphs, generated during multiple compilations with varying optimization settings, forms an ensemble. Software developers may be interested in analyzing this ensemble to gauge how different optimizations affect the application's internal structure. We propose a novel visualization technique that displays ensemble results by linking call graph snapshots at discrete points in the compilation process. This approach accommodates a substantial number of nodes and edges by utilizing a node-link layout with time-based coloring. Furthermore, an interactive interface enables the application of filtering methods to enhance readability, including proximity cuts and dynamic edge labeling. We demonstrate the utility of this method using a set of call graph call graphs generated through diverse optimization combinations in the GCC compiler.

A commonly used benchmark for assessing natural language processing language
models is derived from the CLARIN dataset of the Wikipedia dataset. However, upon
closer inspection, several concerns arise about the data's suitability as a
benchmark, including its limited linguistic diversity, repetitive content, and
the presence of technical vocabulary primarily understood by experts in a
particular field during a specific time period. The paper argues that this data
should not be employed as a standard for evaluating language models.

Observations from the Nançay Radioheliograph are being used to analyze quasi-periodic pulsations (QPP) at the current sheet of a solar flare. A specific solar flare event on 2014 March 29, which was observed by the GOES 15 and SDO, showed QPP in the microwave and X-ray ranges. This event was characterized by a current sheet in the form of an X-shaped loop, and its QPP were found to be caused by the oscillations of the magnetic field lines within this sheet. A distinct pattern of oscillations in the microwave radiation was identified, and it was linked to a specific wave mode in the plasma above the current sheet. This mode corresponds to a particular type of wave known as fast magnetosonic waves, which are the first of their kind to be observed at the current sheet. A mathematical model of these waves has been developed, which suggests that they are the result of the QPP-driven oscillations of the magnetic field lines above the current sheet.

This paper outlines a novel approach for detecting anomalies within images, drawing inspiration from the "A contrario" statistical reasoning method. In contrast to previous methods, which primarily address issues related to security and testing, our technique caters specifically to images within an industrial setting, encompassing various types of artifacts such as defects, scratches, cracks, and burrs. By implementing a multi-scale approach that leverages a set of basic patterns, the method effectively identifies anomalies within images. Notably, it utilizes an advanced statistical model that incorporates image texture information in its decision-making process. Comprehensive testing across various datasets has demonstrated the method's efficacy in detecting anomalies with high accuracy, specifically 98.19% recall and 99.65% precision, with an associated false positive rate of 0.0011 per image.

New well-posedness theorems for a class of higher-order nonlinear equations in both space and time have been established. These theorems apply to solutions with minimal spatial regularity and can handle a broad range of initial conditions. They build on previous research, which showed similar results for a simpler model and provide a significant improvement for a more complex set of equations. Additionally, the theoreums have been extended to include a wider range of initial conditions and can handle a broad spectrum of frequencies.

Kramer's theorem demonstrates degeneracy between two degenerate states in a closed system, even under the influence of an external perturbation, provided the theorem's assumptions are met. In contrast, we find that when a closed system is connected to an environment and driven by an external field, degeneracy can be broken by the presence of the environment alone. Furthermore, under specific conditions, the degeneracy can be restored in both open systems and coupled closed systems, provided the coupling to the environment satisfies certain limitations. Our research also reveals that when a closed system is coupled to an environment, the degeneracy can fail to be violated by the environment, even under strong coupling, provided certain conditions are met.

In highly mobile environments, where base stations frequently reinitializing pilot signals becomes impractical due to excessive overhead, future downlink channel state information can be predicted to optimize data transmission. This study focuses on developing a predictive method combining a deep learning model with a memory model to forecast downlink channel state information without relying on a priori or posteriori channel tracking. By utilizing a limited set of past channel samples as input, the proposed model predicts future channel characteristics, which are then utilized to optimize data transmission. This predictive method achieves significant overhead reductions by 60-80%, resulting in enhanced downlink performance with maximum rate increases of up to 37% over traditional methods.

Regional economic disparities significantly contribute to increased inequality
within countries. However, due to the lack of precise data on regional economic
performance, economists rely heavily on small-area models to derive estimates of
regional economic disparities from available data. This paper presents an alternative
method of using mixtures of beta distributions to estimate regional economic
disparities from large datasets. It is demonstrated that the proposed method
improves estimation precision by reducing variability and achieving faster
convergence rates compared to conventional small-area models. An empirical analysis
of regional unemployment rates across German districts using the German Microcensus
data from 2008-2014 demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms existing
methods by providing more accurate small-area estimates and enabling local level
modelers to adjust the model for regional areas with limited observations.
We establish the scaling approximation formula for the Szeg\H{o} kernel on complex-grassmannian manifolds associated with a Hermitian vector bundle of rank r over a Grauert tube in $\mathbb{C}^N$.

This paper presents an enhanced approach for creating reverse line graphs, known as the Matrix Relabeling Algorithm, MARINLINGA. Compared to the previously established algorithm, the revised method by M. Roussopoulos, our findings show that the MARINLIN GA algorithm is superior, resulting in a significant reduction in the computational time required for implementation.

This paper validates Lee-Lee's hypothesis by demonstrating an equivalence between the roots associated with non-self-intersecting curves in an n-holed disc and the real Schur roots of quivers that have n nodes and are of rank n, plus an additional node.

The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) has become a prevalent platform for developing complex software applications. Notably, Java projects have a high likelihood of relying heavily on external dependencies, which can negatively impact system performance and security. A study examining the Java ecosystem's dependency patterns from 2018 to 2021 reveals concerning trends, including a significant increase in the average number of dependencies per project, and a shift towards utilizing fewer popular, open-source libraries, and more proprietary or unlicensed ones. The findings suggest that this shift may exacerbate existing issues, potentially leading to further project instability.

In this work, a photonic model of control design is presented, which utilizes a novel method combining two distinct states - a biphoton state with entanglement, and a thermal state with mixed phase space properties. By using the biphoton state as an intermediary to establish control relationships, a series of controllable components form a connected network, leading to efficient cooperative behavior. Conversely, a thermal state, due to its lack of control relationships, acts as a disruptive element, hindering the cooperative behavior of the network.

This research develops methods to identify key scenarios in multistage robust optimization problems where uncertainty is distributional, with a focus on improving problem solving efficiency. A scenario selection approach is proposed, grounded in an extension of measure-theoretic total variation distance, that leverages recent developments in empirical quantile estimation. The method can be integrated with existing algorithms for DRO and multi-stage robust optimization problems, including those with continuous and discrete uncertainty distributions. A computational example is provided to demonstrate the efficacy of this scenario selection approach.

Human action anticipation remains a significant challenge in the field of computer vision. Most current research methods rely on a three-phase process: first, a feature extraction phase where essential spatial and temporal features are extracted, followed by a dynamic feature aggregation phase to combine these features, and finally, a classification phase where an anticipation model generates a prediction. However, these sequential processes can be inefficient, slow, and may produce inaccurate anticipation results. To address this limitation, we introduce an innovative model that integrates all three phases into a single, end-to-end model, called the Feature Mapping RNN. By utilizing a kernel-based feature mapping method, we transform the input video data into a high-dimensional space, allowing the model to capture intricate spatio-temporal relationships. Furthermore, we incorporate an attention mechanism to enhance the performance of the model, achieving superior outcomes compared to state-of-the-art methods on diverse human action anticipation datasets.

In the context of quantum thermalization, the process of equilibration can be analyzed by utilizing simple closed systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom that interact with a heat bath. We investigate a model consisting of two coupled harmonic oscillators connected to separate baths at different temperatures, demonstrating that these oscillators equilibrate with different phases at distinct timescales. This phenomenon is rooted in the non-trivial initial conditions, which arise from the baths, rather than the oscillators' internal dynamics. We verify that the phase equilibrium states achieve the same level of detailed balance as observed in the microcanonical or canonical ensembles and confirm that the phase slips resulting from the different phases are absent.

We investigate the properties of pseudo-differential operators on a homogeneous tree by modifying the standard Euclidean definition using a symbol and an operator family. Our analysis focuses on the boundedness and nuclearity of these operators, where we obtain an essential boundedness theorem by developing a new approach in the context of the tree structure. Furthermore, by applying a diagonalization technique inspired by Wiener, we prove that these operators are nuclear by demonstrating their compactness, thereby generalizing previous work related to boundedness on homogeneous trees as outlined in reference [6].

The use of 5G networks has been examined, particularly in terms of how 4G and 5G base stations are structured and how users connect to them. A study was conducted to investigate how 5G technology impacts the way we communicate, especially in comparison to 4G. A comprehensive dataset was collected from a limited number of smartphone participants. It is believed that the results obtained are representative of 5G research areas of interest due to the unique properties of 5G homogenous networks. A total of 1.7 million packets were collected from 5G and 4G networks over a period of 3 days to compare signal strength in different bands. An experiment involving 5G and 5G/4G dual connectivity was also designed to compare performance in terms of packet delivery time and retransmissions. An analysis of the data revealed that 5G exposure is significantly higher than its 4G counterpart. Additionally, the results of the experiment showed that using 5G exclusively results in better performance in terms of lower retransmissions per packet compared to using 5G/4G dual connectivity.

Deep neural networks struggle with accurately identifying out-of-distribution data, particularly when it comes to confidence levels. While some models exhibit overconfidence in such cases, others can be overly cautious, a phenomenon known as underconfidence. To address this issue, a new approach, called the Confidence Out-of-Distribution Examples (CODEs) method, is presented. It aims to improve the confidence levels of a model when encountering ood data by exposing it to a diverse range of examples near its decision boundary. To achieve this, CODEs employs a chamfer distance metric to select examples that are both diverse in terms of distance and similar in terms of class label. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of CODEs in mitigating overconfidence in models, particularly those utilizing softmax, Dirichlet, and Neuronal mixture distributions. Specifically, CODEs exhibits significant improvements in terms of calibration and out-of-distribution detection, particularly when compared to existing approaches.

The CMS experiment at CERN's LHC has measured the distribution of jet arrangements around the most forward energetic jet in 13 TeV proton-proton collisions. The results were compared to perturbative QCD calculations and their precision was enhanced by integrating event data from multiple orifice detectors. The same data was also used to determine the strong coupling constant based on the dependence of jet arrangements on the number of jets, yielding a value of 0.0306 with an error margin of 0.0016.

Deep learning models have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in various computer vision tasks, but their reliance on extensive training data poses a significant challenge in practice. Acquiring large amounts of labeled data is costly and time-consuming. In contrast, the abundance of unlabeled data is often overlooked, making semi-supervised learning and unsupervised learning increasingly important in modern deep learning. This research aims to provide a comprehensive overview of semi-supervised and unsupervised learning techniques in computer vision, with a particular emphasis on those that employ deep learning architectures. We will examine key approaches, including the introduction of fake labels and the manipulation of model regularization. Furthermore, this survey will explore semi-supervised learning in computer vision applications, such as classification and detection, and summarize recent developments in this field. We also explore the potential of self-supervised learning techniques, including auto-encoders and contrastive learning methods. We conclude by discussing the challenges and future research directions in this area.

Identifying anomalies in datasets has become increasingly crucial across various fields, but current techniques often struggle to accurately identify true outliers and false positives, necessitating manually filtered samples. To address this issue, we introduce RECol, a simple yet effective approach based on neural networks that effectively distinguishes between inliers and outliers, utilizing only a single linear layer. Our innovative model utilizes the gradient of predictive functions derived from random neural network mappings of multiple datasets, combined with a novel feature extraction method that enhances the distinction between normal and abnormal data points. Our experimental analysis on 7 datasets reveals that RECol outperforms established methods in precision, precision recall, and AUC scores.

This paper demonstrates the existence of solutions with high-order regularity within a broad class of non-linear Young equations. Furthermore, we establish the global existence of solutions with various levels of regularity, including BV, in a wide class of degenerate and degroding PDEs.

The theoretical implications of recent research on neutrino polarizability are explored in the context of a simple model featuring a dark photon, which has potential implications for a specific type of neutrino oscillation experiment, NuSTAR. An interesting connection is drawn between the dark photon mass and the dark mixing parameter in this model, which has significant implications for a particular neutrino interaction experiment, BEC$^N$.

In the past few years, researchers have made significant efforts to understand the functions of glial cells in the central nervous system, particularly their role in regulating the synapses between neurons. Although glial cells are known to provide metabolic and trophic support to synapses, their presence also leads to heterogeneity in the characteristics of synapses within the same network. This study examines the dynamic relationship between the collective behavior of glial cells and the synchronization of neuronal activity. To do this, a model is developed that describes the interactions between neurons and glial cells within a network, taking into account the effects of different types of synapses and their corresponding connection probabilities. The model reveals that the collective behavior of glial cells can lead to the emergence of rhythmic patterns in the mean firing frequency of neurons, with the effects of excitatory synapses being more pronounced than inhibitory ones. This suggests that the functions of glial cells play a key role in the regulation of collective synaptic activity.

This study explores the unique behavior of a neutral spin-1/2 particle in the presence of a magnetic field by analyzing the Landau levels and geometric phases it experiences. The investigation reveals that this particle exhibits topological properties similar to those of light, and its energy spectrum is characterized by the discrete levels it occupies as it orbits the magnetic field lines. Furthermore, the geometric phases associated with these levels are dependent on the magnetic field strength and the orientation of the particle's orbital angular momentum with respect to the magnetic field. Additionally, the study examines the non-Abelian behavior of the particle's energy levels, which are both topologically and holomorphically significant. The inclusion of the spin-orbit interaction in the particle's Hamiltonian leads to a breakdown in the non-Abelian behavior due to the mixing of the Landau levels, and the associated geometric phases become meaningless.

We've developed a comprehensive theoretical framework to describe how a mobile interface influenced by a random flow is shaped. This interface moves through a stable or unstable environment, and when it reaches certain points, it creates or releases energy, causing changes in the surrounding conditions. Our study uses mathematical models to analyze this process, and we found that under certain conditions, and for a large number of random events, the interface moves at a consistent average rate. Our theory was tested using computer simulations of these random events, and it showed that it can accurately predict how the interface moves even when the energy releases are not evenly spaced. This theoretical framework has broad applications in physics, engineering, and biology, and it particularly applies to the study of crystal growth and the migration of cell membranes.

For a knot in the 3-sphere that forms a Legendrian knot in a contact 3-sphere, we investigate the relationship between its sequence of torsion units and the corresponding hyperbolic volume. It's demonstrated that this knot's unit sequence and torsion units are determined by the corresponding semigroup, known as the formal semigroup. To establish this connection, we utilize the Guckelberger-Vijay-Zemmerich Conjecture which claims that for a knot with a corresponding L-space link and a Legendrian knot, their unit sequence and the formal semigroup are equivalent.

A kinetic theory model is proposed, where particles of varying energies and different species are studied. These particles are located within a finite, confined space. A novel approach is presented, which involves mapping the kinetic theory of this particle ensemble to a hydrodynamic model using a Poisson map. This transformation establishes a set of hydrodynamic fields and their relationships. A set of equations governing this model is provided, which includes energy and entropy conservation. Importantly, this model is non-equilibrium in terms of entropy, with a method for calculating its evolution provided. A new statistical mechanical framework for understanding non-equilibrium systems is introduced. A relation between the kinetic theory and the hydrodynamic model is established through a Poisson map, which is valid for long-term averages. This map is used to derive a non-equilibrium equation for the evolution of entropy, as well as relations for energy and particle density evolution. A key aspect of this model is its ability to capture the effects of finite spatial dimensions on kinetic theory. This is achieved by using a constant surface energy density. A new approach is proposed, which involves a non-equilibrium partition function that is valid for finite systems. This partition function is used to derive a relation between the kinetic theory and the hydrodynamic model. A set of hydrodynamic fields and their relationships is established, which includes energy and particle density fields. A set of equations governing this model is derived, which includes energy and particle density conservation. A relation between the kinetic theory and the hydrodynamic model is

In the context of endoscopic video, the challenge of artifact detection can be overcome by applying object detection methods. However, the performance of these methods is often compromised by the complex and dynamic nature of endoscopy, which involves variations in appearance, motion, and scale. To address this issue, this study explores the potential of combining the predictions of multiple object detectors, trained on distinct subsets of the same dataset, in order to enhance the robustness of their performance. The experiment involves training a range of object detectors, including Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, and EfficientDet, on the publicly available MIAS dataset, which splits into five subsets. The results indicate that combining the predictions of multiple models, trained on different subsets, outperforms the performance of a single model trained on the entire dataset.

Research has extensively studied the grammar patterns present in programming languages, specifically in identifier names and comments, employing both traditional methods and NLP techniques. This study investigates the grammar patterns found in a large dataset of identifiers from 28 different programming languages, examining the relationships between these patterns and their meanings. We categorize the discovered grammar patterns into three types: structural, semantic, and functional. The results show that, contrary to our expectations, a substantial number of these patterns, classified as functional, may actually be associated with linguistic features such as first names, surnames, and well-known people, rather than any actual software functions. The study also reveals that, across the evaluated languages, a notable proportion of these patterns, approximately 20%, are shared among all the languages, suggesting that they may represent a common set of patterns found in many different languages.

We create a module based on the $q$-differential operator algebra by using the $q$-shuffle algebra associated with affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. This module is isomorphic to the $q$-integers module for $q$ in the range from 0 to 1 not including its endpoints. We also investigate the growth characteristics of the dimension of the space of invariants for the braided Hopf structure on the $q$-differential operator algebra when the parameter $q$ varies.

The evolution of polycrystalline systems is significantly influenced by the growth of grains, which in turn affects the microstructure's overall properties. To gain a deeper understanding of this process, we employed a data-driven approach to analyze the kinetics of grain growth in various systems. By utilizing a novel machine learning based method, we investigated the effects of different grain-pair interactions on grain growth in a two-grain system, and then extended our analysis to more complex scenarios involving multiple grain types and phases. In particular, we focused on grain growth in a three-grain system, and later in a duplex system consisting of two-grain and triplex grain mixtures. Our findings revealed that grain growth kinetics is primarily governed by the interaction between the grain and its neighbors, which is influenced by the grain types involved, and to a lesser extent, by the interaction between the grain and the surrounding matrix. A key discovery was that grain growth in a triplex system is significantly influenced by the grain types present in the initial mixture, which can lead to grain growth inhibition or acceleration. Our data-driven analysis also enabled us to identify the dominant grain types in different regions of the microstructure, which in turn affected the grain growth rate. Overall, our study provides a deeper understanding of how grain-pair interactions govern the evolution of microstructure during grain growth.

Human pose and shape estimation techniques have been advancing quickly, but existing evaluations primarily focus on comparing different algorithms. In an effort to improve the state-of-the-art method, various datasets with controlled factors have been proposed to assess algorithmic differences. However, considering the real-world settings where data is often biased and inconsistent, it is crucial to understand the impact of such factors. In this research, we examine the influence of data collection methods, model types, and pre-training models on existing pose and shape estimation benchmarks, revealing significant effects on performance outcomes. Our study highlights the real-world performance of top-performing models in a challenging in-the-wild dataset, demonstrating that their performance is below expected levels. The findings suggest that current benchmarks have significant flaws and need to be reassessed.

Within the framework of microscopic theory of superconductivity, it's demonstrated that near-singular points where an attractive electron-electron interaction becomes weakly repulsive, the superconductivity characteristics (critical temperature, gap function, and condensate density phase) remain virtually unchanged for an extremely diluted system of interacting particles. These findings are supported by applying the Ginzburg-Landau theory to the gap function and analyzing how phase transitions between different superconducting states occur. In a two-dimensional near-singular case, the presence of two distinct superconducting states, s-wave and p-wave, is established, with the s-wave state being the thermodynamic ground state.

We introduce a comprehensive scalar leptoquark action that can be used to calculate corrections in the electroweak effective theory. This theory enables the computation of two- and four-point diagrams, including those of order dim6, and provides a basis for the calculation of higher-order graphs. By using this theory, we can derive the universal matching conditions for the dim8 operators, which can then be used to predict the magnitude of dim8 corrections in various leptoquark models. Our approach can be extended to compute higher-order diagrams across multiple models.

Machine learning has become omnipresent in the tech sphere, transforming various aspects of science, engineering, and technology. At the heart of this phenomenon is the widespread application of mathematical structures, with category theory being a pivotal element in their theoretical underpinnings. In this review, we explore the historical context of category theory's role in machine learning, its significance in framing machine learning theory, and its current applications within the field.

This study presents an innovative terminal sliding mode control strategy tailored specifically for second-order motion systems. Building on standard sliding mode control principles, TSM controllers leverage a sliding surface that converges to zero within a finite period. Despite TSM controllers' high noise-hiding capabilities, their excessive chattering issue persists. To address this limitation, optimal TSM control is developed, leveraging an Itô-Karp type optimal control system to minimize chattering. An accompanying solution is derived, and numerical case studies have been conducted to validate the new approach.

Lithium-ion batteries are being utilized extensively in electric vehicles, where they are subjected to high cyclic loads, prolonged lifespan requirements, and safety concerns. Consequently, it is essential to develop non-destructive methods for assessing the internal functioning of these batteries during their operational lifespan. Our research involves employing ultrasonic resonance techniques to investigate the layered structure within a lithium-ion battery cell, focusing on both longitudinal and layer modulations. The results reveal that the cell's layered structure can be characterized using power spectral analysis and signal processing. Moreover, our findings suggest that the layer modulations are sensitive to the prevalence of pre-existing defects, such as electrode cracks, which can impede the battery's performance.

This study focuses on designing a discrete-time tracking control system for a gantry crane using flatness-based methods. The model is developed based on the crane's dynamic equations, and a proposed control law is tested in a simulation environment utilizing a crane with mass characteristics similar to those of an Airbus A380. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the discrete-time tracking control system in navigating the gantery crane to desired positions.

Significant advancements in generating concise captions for images have been achieved through joint training of vision and language models. However, conventional training data collection methods often lead to captions containing noise, primarily because human evaluators have differing opinions on how to accurately describe an image. This issue causes models to produce captions lacking coherence or which are simply too long. Existing techniques for handling such noise rely on regularizers that penalize models producing repetitive captions. In contrast, our novel approach, cooperative distillation, identifies and mitigates caption noise by synchronizing the hidden states of two pre-trained models. This is achieved by generating captions using both models' captions and selecting those where the relative order is consistent. Experimental results on the MSCOCO dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art image captioning models, producing more accurate, high-quality captions.

A collection $\mathcal{I}$ of strings is considered well-connected within a given alphabet if a string of maximum length is created by concatenating all strings in $\mathcal{I}$. In 2009, a paper by Galil et al. introduced the concept of well-connected sets, however did not provide a method to identify them efficiently. Later, in 2016, a counterexample was discovered showing that determining the largest well-connected set of n strings could not be done in linear time, a phenomenon known as the "worst case." In contrast, a new study presents an efficient algorithm running in O(n^5) time and O(n^4) space, allowing for the computation of a well-connected set of n strings in linear time. Additionally, a more efficient algorithm running in O(n^3) time can be achieved by using a more efficient data structure.

Ehresmann semigroups extend the concept of monoids by incorporating a binary operation with a left and right identity, allowing the right identity to be absent. These semigroups can be categorized into three types: those resembling two-sided semigroups, one-sided semigroups where one identity is absent, and multiplicative semigroups where the left and right identities coincide. Categories may be viewed as a special type of Ehresmann semigroup. This study delves into ordered Ehresmann semigroups, a subset that meets specific properties, including the preservation of binary operation order, allowing for a right identity that fulfills certain constraints, and the inclusion of an absorbing element. Ordered categories are also explored, along with other related concepts, with a focus on their properties, including the preservation of binary operation order, the inclusion of a minimal element, and the presence of a unique join. These concepts are further analyzed through examples of ordered Ehresmann semigroups.

Recent self-attention models have achieved top-notch performance in natural language processing tasks, yet their performance is heavily reliant on the chosen depth and width. This research delves into the interplay between depth and width in self-attention models, revealing that increasing the depth can be hindered by low width and vice versa. We pinpoint the cause of this issue, which is computationally expensive training due to the similarity between subsequent self-attention layers. To tackle this problem, we introduce a computational expense metric. To overcome the performance limitations, we develop a new training approach that accelerates the computation by reducing intermediate token similarity. This method involves modifying the input tokens and introducing a new training objective. Our proposed approach is tested on the Transformer model and evaluated using the GLUE benchmark dataset, resulting in significantly improved performance. Additionally, we demonstrate that our approach can accelerate the training process without performance degradation when combining the Transformer model with a deeper architecture.

A novel method was developed to synthesize BiFeO$_{3}$ nanoparticles, with temperature playing a key role in the formation of its surface bi-oxide and iron oxide layers. The particles produced via a lower temperature process showed enhanced magnetic and catalytic properties, including a higher saturation magnetization of 0.12 emu/g and a faster rate in hydrogen production of 0.154 m mol $\cdot$ $R.S.V.P.$ $\cdot$ day. Utilizing a soft-chemistry approach, the particles were synthesized at temperatures ranging from 300-600 $\degree$C. The optimal conditions for the formation of a bi-oxide surface layer was found to be at 450 $\degree$C, with this layer enhancing the magnetic and catalytic properties of the particles. The particles produced at this temperature showed a higher saturation magnetization of 0.12 emu/g, and demonstrated superior performance in hydrogen production, with an efficiency of 0.154 m mol $\cdot$ $R.S.V.P.$ $\cdot$ day. The particles produced at 450 $\degree$C also showed a more effective degradation of Rhodamine B, with a higher efficiency of 0.45 $\cdot$ day. Using the masses of the bottom quark and the tau lepton in a simplified ${\rm SU}(6)$ model with massless ${\rm U}(1)_Y$ gauge bosons, we find specific mass terms. The model includes a mass difference between the two particles, which can be attributed to the difference in their electric charges in the ${\rm SU}(6)$ framework.
